abstract: Maintains deep reservoir temperature sounding and fault slip stability evaluations
system_message:
You are the Hydrogeological engineering lead (GEO), responsible for maintaining deep reservoir temperature soundings and fault slip stability evaluations across prospective geothermal exploratory drilling sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: measured after complete thermal shut-in equilibration·Maintains deep reservoir temperature sounding and fault slip stability evaluations（RES）
information_points.content:
GEO-RES-J6S：For Bruchsal Bedrock Outlier, under the measurement basis measured after complete thermal shut-in equilibration, the geothermal reservoir bottom-hole temperature at the 3500 m target reservoir zone is 145 degC, and fault slip stability certification is verified for major bounding faults within a 5 km radius.
GEO-RES-LT5：For Rheintal Fault Basin, under the measurement basis measured after complete thermal shut-in equilibration, the geothermal reservoir bottom-hole temperature at the 3500 m target reservoir zone is 155 degC, and fault slip stability certification for major bounding faults within a 5 km radius is confirmed.
GEO-RES-4G2：For Landau Sandstone Terrace, evaluated with the measurement basis measured after complete thermal shut-in equilibration, the geothermal reservoir bottom-hole temperature at the 3500 m target reservoir zone is 125 degC, and fault slip stability certification is confirmed for major bounding faults within 5 km.

information_points.title: measured before complete thermal shut-in equilibration·Maintains deep reservoir temperature sounding and fault slip stability evaluations（MIN）
information_points.content:
GEO-MIN-UNA：For Landau Sandstone Terrace, based on the measurement basis measured before complete thermal shut-in equilibration, the geothermal reservoir bottom-hole temperature at the 3500 m target reservoir zone is 125 degC, and fault slip stability certification is confirmed.
GEO-MIN-54O：For Bruchsal Bedrock Outlier, under the measurement basis measured before complete thermal shut-in equilibration, the geothermal reservoir bottom-hole temperature at the 3500 m target reservoir zone is 145 degC, and fault slip stability certification is confirmed for major bounding faults within 5 km.
GEO-MIN-ACZ：For Rheintal Fault Basin, under the measurement basis measured before complete thermal shut-in equilibration, the geothermal reservoir bottom-hole temperature at the 3500 m target reservoir zone is 145 degC, and fault slip stability certification is not confirmed.
